questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to visit a nice city. Barcelona has so many great things to offer: cultural activities, beautiful weather, cool bars/restaurants, and friendly people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was originally planning to do an exchange stay in Australia but because of the pandemic, I had to come up with an alternative plan. Despite this, I could not imagine a better exchange stay and I am really happy that I ended up going to Barcelona.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The faculty held a welcome session which was primarily directed towards bachelor students. However, the international office helped answer any questions I had as a master student. Later, when the trimester started, the master's degree held a welcome session as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, the international office helped answer any questions I had as a master student. This was mostly related to the courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
First, I joined different facebook groups for people looking for housing in Barcelona. However, I found it a bit stressful and decided to book a room through
spotahome.com
which worked well, especially because they make videos of the apartments which is nice when you are not able to go there yourself. The downside is that you do not know who you will be living with.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it worked really well. Most people I have met (if not all) in the master's degree live/lived off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: From my experience, it is easier to find housing in Barcelona than it is in Copenhagen. Also, there are good options for people staying for only a short period of time (e.g. exchange students).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Few course numbers/names changed before the trimester so I had to obtain a new pre-approval. However, it was a minor thing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I looked at previous years' schedules and tried to find courses that did not overlap with courses that I took at home. The international office helped me registre the courses and they were very flexible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office was very helpful and replied quickly to my mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I advice you to contact the international office if you run into problems.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sometimes I found it a bit confusing as to what exactly was expected from us students. The reading lists in some courses were less clear than at KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses were similar to those at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it depends on the specific course. In some courses, the teaching style was similar to those of the courses at KU while in other courses, the teaching style was more interactive.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Regional and Urban Economics, Cooperative Decisions and Social Choice, Governments and Markets, and Public Economics II.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think the course Regional and Urban Economics was pretty good. It was well-structured. However, the work load was a bit heavy compared to the other courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ate out a little more than expected. I'm not completely sure about the amount spent on food.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Good coffee was cheaper than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were introduced to the sport facilities at the welcome session but I did not use them. Therefore, I do not know how satisfied I would have been with them. At the welcome session, ESN presented and they hosted a range of nice events.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I mostly went to ESN events (e.g. parties, beach volley, and day trips to beautiful places outside the city). It was a really easy way to meet people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The above mentioned with ESN.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Costa Brava and Mont Rebei.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. I do not speak Spanish or Catalan but you quickly learn the essentials.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The master's degree is very international so it was no problem that I did not speak Spanish or Catalan. There are quite few people in the master's degree, so everyone gets to know each other.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: If anything, the language. But as mentioned above, it was no problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food is amazing and people are really friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it, maybe consider taking a language course (I kind of wish I did), and download WhatsApp!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join different WhatsApp groups - a lot of communication happens there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The personal development that comes with it. Also, I feel just as comfortable speaking English as Danish now which is nice.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe finding the right balance between studies and social life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I really recommend going on exchange in general and to Barcelona specifically. It has really been a great experience :-)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
